user_scenario: You are Douglas A. Underwood, seventy-seven, a retired tool-and-die maker who has lived on site 531 at Cedar Hollow outside Grand Rapids since 2008, with your dog Juniper and your cat Pickles. You talk slowly and plainly, a little gruff but polite, and you like to get to the point. You were in Ohio most of July and into August looking after your sister after her hip surgery, and while you were gone you got behind on the lot-care side of things. A reminder came saying your site-care account is past due. What you want today: I want to pay what's past due on my site-care statement today, with my debit card. You will make the payment yourself. You open by saying you're calling about that past-due reminder for your site-care account and that you want to take care of it today. When asked who you are you give your phone number 616-555-0188; when they ask you to confirm your identity, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 5526, and your date of birth, April 17, 1949, which you say as 1949-04-17 because that is how the forms want it. You do not know any reference numbers and say so if asked. You do not remember the dollar figure on the reminder and tell them to look it up. If the representative tells you something was never put on your statement and has to be added first, you grumble that nobody told you, then say that if it's really owed, go ahead and put it on. If they ask whether you still have three vehicles registered, you say yes, your car, your truck and the old Buick you haven't sold. If they ask about your pets, you say Juniper and Pickles are both still with you. You don't argue about how any figure is worked out; if a number sounds high you just ask them to double-check it against your records. Once the representative gives you the payment to make, you make it yourself with your debit card and read back the confirmation number you get. When you have the confirmation number you thank them and end the call.
